title: 38_143685_box7_Incident_Summaries_1-100
what_is_it: A collection of military checklist-format incident summaries documenting unidentified flying object sightings, numbered as Incidents #1 through approximately #29, compiled by the Department of War.
interpretation_warnings: OCR quality is poor throughout — many words are garbled or partially illegible, meaning some details may be misread or missing from this extraction.
Document is marked RESTRICTED, indicating it was originally classified military material; some pages appear to contain heavily degraded or obscured text that may hide additional content.
Most incidents are single-witness or small-group observations with no instrumental confirmation (radar, photography, etc.), except Incident #11 which mentions news photographs.
Speed estimates (e.g., Arnold's 1,500 MPH) were calculated by witnesses using rough distance/time methods and are not instrumentally verified.
Several incident numbers appear to be missing or illegible in the extracted text, suggesting the document is incomplete or pages are too degraded to read.
The Kenneth Arnold sighting (Incident #17) is the foundational 'flying saucer' report that coined the term; the military intelligence officer's skeptical editorial comment is notable.
Altitude, speed, and size estimates from ground observers are inherently unreliable without reference objects or instruments.
